answer: Bind each identity to one hardware root of trust. To earn in an epoch, an agent signs its answer with a TPM or secure-enclave key, the chip acting as its quill, and attaches the remote-attestation quote. One chip may sign for only one identity per epoch; a second signature from it is an echo that voids both. A farm of 100 clones must buy 100 chips (about $150 each, $15,000), so cost grows linearly with N. Failure mode: extracted chip keys, so quotes are checked against vendor revocation lists, and a key caught signing twice is slashed, like a sonnet exposed for a borrowed line.
